Ionawr 6 1854        David Roberts

Fy Hanes

Wele a ganlyn sydd ychydig o'm hachau fel y gallais eu cael.

Ganwyd fi yn y flwyddyn 1814 Ebrill y 5 yn Sir Feirionydd yn y Nanmor mewn ty a elwir y Rhos hwn ar hen etifeddiaeth yr enwog Arglwydd Dafydd Nanmor (yr hwn y lle yn awr ag Beddgelert yn Sir Gaernarfon). Ganwyd wyth o blant i'n rhieni, sef Robert (bu farw yn dri mis oed), Edward, Robert, Elinor, David, William, Daniel, a John Roberts. Y pump hynaf a anwyd yn y Tanyrallt, a'r ddau nesaf yn Brynygwyngyll, a'r mab ieuengaf John yn y Llety yn mhlwyf Llanfrothen.

Edward a briodwyd ag Elinor Griffith, merch i Griffith a Chatherine Williams, Bronyforllan, yn Llanfrothen.

Robert a briodwyd yn Llanfrothen a Gwen, merch i William a Mary Williams, Cae Glas, Llanfrothen; ganed 12 o blant iddynt.

Elinor a briodwyd a John, mab i William Humphrey a Chatherine James, plwyf Festiniog. Ganwyd iddi naw o blant; ymfudasant i America.

Myfi David a briodwyd yn Llanfrothen a Chathreina, merch i Thomas Richards ac Ann Morris, y Creua Mawr, Llanfrothen. Ganwyd i ni chwech o blant, yr hynaf Robert, Thomas, David, Ann, Elizabeth a Jane Roberts.

William a briodwyd a Margred, merch i Evan Roberts a Jane Griffith, y Gair y Rallt bach. Ganwyd iddynt bedwar o blant, Elizabeth, Robert, Evan a William Roberts; yr ieuengaf a fu farw yn faban.

Daniel a briodwyd yn Llanfrothen a Gwen, merch i John Lloyd a Chatherine [continues on PDF page 69]
journalPages.translation:
January 6, 1854        David Roberts

My history

Behold, what follows is a little of my ancestry, as I was able to obtain it.

I was born on April 5, 1814, in Merionethshire, in Nanmor, in a house called Rhos, on the old estate of the renowned Lord Dafydd Nanmor (the place is now associated with Beddgelert in Caernarfonshire). Eight children were born to our parents: Robert, who died at three months old; Edward; Robert; Elinor; David; William; Daniel; and John Roberts. The five eldest were born at Tanyrallt, the next two at Brynygwyngyll, and the youngest son, John, at Llety in the parish of Llanfrothen.

Edward married Elinor Griffith, daughter of Griffith and Chatherine Williams of Bronyforllan in Llanfrothen.

Robert married Gwen in Llanfrothen. She was the daughter of William and Mary Williams of Cae Glas, Llanfrothen. Twelve children were born to them.

Elinor married John, son of William Humphrey and Chatherine James of the parish of Festiniog. Nine children were born to her; they emigrated to America.

I, David, married Chathreina, daughter of Thomas Richards and Ann Morris of Creua Mawr, Llanfrothen. Six children were born to us: the eldest, Robert, followed by Thomas, David, Ann, Elizabeth, and Jane Roberts.

William married Margred, daughter of Evan Roberts and Jane Griffith of Gair y Rallt bach. Four children were born to them: Elizabeth, Robert, Evan, and William Roberts; the youngest died as an infant.

Daniel married Gwen in Llanfrothen, daughter of John Lloyd and Chatherine [continues on PDF page 69].
journalPages.notes:
The page begins a clean first-person ancestry entry dated January 6, 1854 and headed `Fy Hanes`. The named `David Roberts`, first-person marriage statement, contemporaneous date, and continuous compact hand support David Roberts as probable content author and probable scribe. No separate signature or independently attributable handwriting exemplar makes the physical hand confirmed.

The entry continues directly onto Welsh PDF page 69. It has a confirmed historical-English parallel on RDR PDF page 3. RDR is a close translation with paraphrase and normalization of several names and places. The Welsh manuscript remains primary: source forms including `Chatherine`, `Chathreina`, `Margred`, `Bronyforllan`, `Brynygwyngyll`, and `Gair y Rallt bach` are preserved rather than replaced by RDR forms.

Coherent comparison across pages 68-72 confirms the opening locality as `Nanmor` and the lord's name as `Dafydd Nanmor` from the Welsh letterforms. RDR instead supplies `Parish of Festiniog` and `Lord Dudley Nanney`; that conflict remains recorded rather than harmonized. The Welsh manuscript gives David's birth date as April 5, 1814, while RDR page 3 gives April 14, 1814; both source readings are preserved.

No hymn, song, poetry, composition, or publication reference appears on this page.

Now I shall think a little about my own history.

I was raised amid great poverty. The ordinary laborer's wage was my father's wage, which for many years was from one shilling to one shilling and sixpence a day, while also feeding himself; this was often too little to obtain bread for the family. My tasks until I was about eleven were [unclear: begging or driving], gathering lichen, scraping oak bark, and [unclear occupational term], and similar things, each in its season.

I was very ill with ague when I was between ten and eleven, and soon after recovering I went to the quarry with my father and my brother Robert at Festiniog. I continued the work of dressing slate under many disadvantages until I was fifteen or sixteen. At that time I went to a place called Cae, next to the Cwmstradlyn valley, to work for a man named William Hughes. I remained there about a year and a half, then returned to the quarry; and from then until now I have followed one branch or another of quarry work.

No one considered [unclear: that I needed day school], and I received very little of it. My parents sent me to the Calvinistic Methodist Sunday school, where I began to read Welsh. My inclination was toward the Baptists, and consequently I was [unclear: resistant] to attending their schools; and the Baptists did not [unclear: maintain] a school, because they considered [unclear: teaching] a sin.

Bethania Ionawr 18 - 1856

Yr oeddwn i dair ar hugain oed oeddwn pan briodais Catherine. I fyw i [unclear: Haffty y Moelwyn] Park, Llanfrothen, am y flwyddyn gyntaf. Myfi a genhedlwyd i ffydd yr Efengyl gan Robert Evans, Glan Conwy, ac a fedyddiwyd ganddo yn afon y Pandy gerllaw Gelli Cwmstradlyn, ar y 24 dydd o Fis Mai yn y flwyddyn 1846. Ac a gadarnhawyd gan Abel Evans. Ac yn fuan derbyniais yr Offeiriadaeth Santaidd. Gosodwyd ar fy ysgwyddau y ddyledswydd bwysig o bregethu yr Efengyl dragwyddol yng nghyflawnder ei bendithion. Ac ymddiriedwyd yn fy ngofal Gangen o Eglwys Iesu Grist a elwir Cangen Festiniog. Cefais y fraint i letya yn fy nhy lawer o weision Crist, a'u cynorthwyo gyda dillad ac arian i adeiladu Teyrnas Iesu Grist fy Arglwydd.

Chathreina fy ngwraig a fedyddiwyd gan David Peters ger y Rhydfudr, Festiniog, Awst 22 - 1846.

Ein plant a fedyddiwyd gennyf. Thomas, Medi 30 - 1849. Daniel a fedyddiwyd Medi 17 - 1850 yn ei wyth mlwydd oed. Ann a fedyddiwyd Rhagfyr 28 - 1852 yn ei hawyth mlwydd oed. [Continues on PDF page 72.]
journalPages.translation:
[Unclear: the grandmother] of Gwilym Ystradau the Bard, where he too was lodging. He was nearly the same age and had the same inclination toward poetry; therefore we were of some encouragement to one another. We became acquainted with the old bard [unclear: Gryffyn Davy] and received some lessons from him.

Bethania, January 18, 1856

I was twenty-three years old when I married Catherine. We went to live at [unclear: Haffty y Moelwyn] Park, Llanfrothen, for the first year. From there we moved to Gelli Cwmstradlyn, in the same parish and on the same estate; from Gelli to [unclear place], parish of Festiniog; from [that place] to Dol y Garreg Ddu in the same parish; and from Dol y Garreg Ddu to Bethania, where we are now. We intend to emigrate to America (or Utah) between now and the beginning of next March.

I was brought to faith in the Gospel by Robert Evans of Glan Conwy and was baptized by him in the River Pandy near Gelli Cwmstradlyn on May 24, 1846. I was confirmed by Abel Evans, and soon received the Holy Priesthood. The important duty of preaching the everlasting Gospel in the fulness of its blessings was placed upon my shoulders. A branch of the Church of Jesus Christ called the Festiniog Branch was entrusted to my care. I had the privilege of lodging many servants of Christ in my house and assisting them with clothing and money to build the Kingdom of Jesus Christ my Lord.

My wife Chathreina was baptized by David Peters near Rhydfudr, Festiniog, on August 22, 1846.

Our children were baptized by me: Thomas, September 30, 1849; Daniel was baptized September 17, 1850, at eight years old; and Ann was baptized December 28, 1852, at eight years old. [Continues on PDF page 72.]

Y mae Robert heb ei fedyddio er ei fod yn credu yr Efengyl. Ac y mae Jane heb ei fedyddio oherwydd ei bod o dan oedran.

Ganwyd fy Ngwraig yn y Creua Mawr, Llanfrothen. Enw ei Thad, fel y soniwyd uchod, Thomas Richards; enw ei mam, Ann Morris. Ei Thad a fagwyd gyda ei nain yn y Creua. Enw ei dad oedd Richard Thomas; enw ei fam oedd Elizabeth. Enwau ei daid a'i nain oedd Thomas Williams a Chathreina uch Richard.

Enwau plant Richard ac Elizabeth Thomas fel y canlyn: Thomas, Chathreina, Robert a Jane Richards.

Enwau plant Thomas Richards ac Ann Morris fel y canlyn: Jane, Chathreina a Richard Thomas.

Ann Morris, gwraig Thomas Richards, a anwyd yn Llwyn yr Hwch, Llanfrothen. Enw ei Thad Rowland Morris; enw ei mam oedd Jane Parry. Enwau plant Rowland a Jane Parry fel y canlyn: Rowland, Janet, Ann, Elinor, Henry Morris.

Enwau fy Nhad a mam ydynt Robert Roberts ac Elizabeth Edwards. Hwy a briodwyd yn Beddgelert yn y flwyddyn 1806, y 3 dydd o Chwefror. Ganwyd fy Nhad mewn Cae Glas, Clynog, yn Sir Gaernarfon yn y flwyddyn 1775, ar y 18 dydd o Ionawr. Ganwyd i'w rieni naw o blant fel y canlyn: Salmon, Margred, Robert (fy Nhad), Catherine, Jane, Ann, Elinor, Elizabeth a William Roberts. Fy nhaid a anwyd yn Felin Faesog, Clynog.
journalPages.translation:
Elizabeth was baptized April 9, 1855.

Robert has not been baptized, although he believes the Gospel. Jane has not been baptized because she is under age.

My wife was born at Creua Mawr, Llanfrothen. Her father, as mentioned above, was Thomas Richards; her mother was Ann Morris. Her father was raised with his grandmother at Creua. His father was Richard Thomas and his mother was Elizabeth. His grandfather and grandmother were Thomas Williams and Chathreina uch Richard.

The names of the children of Richard and Elizabeth Thomas were as follows: Thomas, Chathreina, Robert, and Jane Richards.

The names of the children of Thomas Richards and Ann Morris were as follows: Jane, Chathreina, and Richard Thomas.

Ann Morris, wife of Thomas Richards, was born at Llwyn yr Hwch, Llanfrothen. Her father was Rowland Morris and her mother was Jane Parry. The names of the children of Rowland and Jane Parry were as follows: Rowland, Janet, Ann, Elinor, and Henry Morris.

The names of my father and mother are Robert Roberts and Elizabeth Edwards. They were married at Beddgelert on February 3, 1806. My father was born at Cae Glas, Clynog, in Caernarfonshire on January 18, 1775. Nine children were born to his parents, as follows: Salmon, Margred, Robert (my father), Catherine, Jane, Ann, Elinor, Elizabeth, and William Roberts. My grandfather was born at Felin Faesog, Clynog.

Logan City April 17 1886

Genealogy of Elizabeth Roberts

Her parents names are David R Roberts and Catherine Thomas she was born [unclear: November 13] in the year 1846 in Cwm y Gelli Parish of Festiniog County of Merioneth North Wales she has been baptised by her father David R Roberts and very likely confirmed by the same April 9 the year 1855.

### Entry 2: David R Roberts autobiography

[unclear: Gelli, Davis] Farmington Feb 4th 1858.

Genealogy of David R Roberts. My native land is North Wales my Father was born in Clynog Caernarvonshire and my Mother both in Caernarvon Shire [unclear: she was born in Beddgelert]. I was born in a house called [unclear: Bron y Garth] in a place named [unclear: Nantmor] in Merioneth Shire but as I have said reside with Caernarvon since long time. I was born on the sixth of April 1814 and Married in the year 1837 in the Parish of Llanfrothen Merionethshire North Wales and I was Baptised May 24th in 1846 by Robert Evans Glan Conwy and in June 21st being Confirmed by Abel Evans March in Priest and soon after that to be an Elder and emigrated from the old country on the 13th of April in the 1856 and arrived the Valley on the 2nd Oct 1856.

journalPages.notes:
Page 73 does not continue page 72. It contains two distinct English entries in different hands and from different writing moments.

The upper entry is dated April 17, 1886, concerns Elizabeth Roberts, and is explicitly signed `Robert D Roberts`. Robert D. Roberts is therefore the confirmed content author and scribe of that entry. The account is retrospective and records events from 1846, 1855, and 1869.

The lower entry is dated February 4, 1858, is written in the first person as a genealogy/autobiography of David R Roberts, and is explicitly signed `David R Roberts`. David R. Roberts is therefore the confirmed content author and scribe of that entry. Its date precedes David Roberts's death on November 4, 1858. The hand differs from the upper Robert D. Roberts entry and is broadly consistent with the compact early Welsh block on pages 68-72, but the signature and first-person self-identification provide the direct attribution evidence.

The lower entry supplies an independent manuscript witness for April 6, 1814 as David Roberts's birth date. This agrees with the day visible in Welsh on page 68 and conflicts with the April 14 date in the later RDR historical English account; the disagreement is preserved rather than harmonized.

The RDR journal contains related family-history material, but no passage located in the completed transcription is a close page-level duplicate of these two entries. RDR page 23 independently records Robert D. Roberts's April 4, 1858 baptism by his father David R. Roberts; that is contextual corroboration, not a parallel for the events transcribed here.

Logan City, January 2, 1861.

I will give a little of our history from the old country up to the present, as correctly as my memory allows. We left Bethania, Ffestiniog, on April 14, 1856, and reached Liverpool. On the nineteenth of the same month we went aboard the ship *S. Curling*, which began its journey across the Atlantic the following day. The voyage was very rough, with the sea rising greatly. We reached the American continent on May 24, [unclear in Welsh] Boston. After a day or two we took the railroad to Iowa City, where we remained for nearly three weeks. From there we began our journey across the plains with handcarts to Utah.

We stayed for a few days in Salt Lake City after arriving on October 2. The journey was very hard because we did not have half enough food, and pulling the handcart was hard. After several days my father and the [unclear in Welsh] went to Farmington, eighteen miles north of Salt Lake City. I then went twenty-two miles farther to Ogden with Erastus Bingham and remained there for four [unclear in Welsh], after which I returned to my father, my mother, my brothers, and my sisters.

Logan City, November 5, 1869

On Monday afternoon, October 11, in the year 1869, Elizabeth, our sister and the wife of Taliesin Hughes, gave birth to twins, a boy and a girl, but they lived only a short time. Elizabeth had been unwell while arranging her brother-in-law's bed, which was required to be in a high place; this caused their premature birth. Elizabeth has recovered exceptionally well. We give their names as James and Margaret Hughes.

They intend to go to Salt Lake City at the end of the year to be washed and anointed in the house of the Lord on [unclear in Welsh: the twenty-first] (22) of November 1869. They live in Meadow Valley, Sevier County, Utah Territory.

R. D. Roberts

Logan City, January 1870

There is an error in the account above concerning the twins; their names are James and Cathrina, Cathrina having the same name as the mother of Elizabeth, our sister.

On November 22, 1869, instead of the fifteenth (15), they were [unclear in Welsh: consecrated] in the house of the Lord in Salt Lake City.

Logan City, July 12, 1870

On June 1, 1870, I set out for Smithfield to fetch Hannah Roberts and returned to Logan. The next day I set out for Salt Lake City and arrived there on the fourth. On the sixth we went to the House of the Lord to be united for time and eternity by Joseph F. Smith, one of the Apostles and a son of Hyrum Smith the patriarch. Hugh and Mary Roberts are Hannah's parents. At present they live in Smithfield, Cache County, Utah Territory. They emigrated from Eglwys bach, Pembrokeshire, Wales, to Salt Lake City in the year 1864.

Robert David Roberts

Hannah Roberts was born March 27, 1847, at Eglwys bach, Pembrokeshire.

R. D. Roberts

January 4, 1871

Ann, our sister, gave birth to a fine son at six [unclear in Welsh: in the morning], weighing ten pounds. His name was David Roberts Hopkin. He was blessed by [unclear: Benjamin M. Munnon] on May 4, 1871.

Elizabeth, our sister, gave birth to twin girls on February 8, 1871, at Farmington, Utah, Davis County. Their names were Ann and Margaret. February 21. Daniel Roberts, my brother, was rebaptized by Robert Davidson; he was confirmed by Thomas McNeil, senior.

gave birth to a girl who appeared to have a strong constitution, weighing nine pounds. On October 5 she was blessed in Logan by Thomas Jones; her name is Cathreina Roberts.

Jane Hughes, our sister, gave birth to a boy at fifteen minutes past nine (9:15) in the morning in Samaria, Oneida County, Idaho Territory. He was blessed on February 11, 1877, by Owen Thomas; his name is James Hughes. At one month old he weighed eleven pounds.

January 23, 1877

At twenty-five minutes past eleven (11:25) in the morning, Elizabeth Hughes, our sister and the wife of Taliesin Hughes, gave birth to a girl in Samaria, Oneida County, Idaho Territory. She was blessed on February 18 by Owen Thomas; her name is Maria Hughes.

May 16, 1877

Daniel, in Ogden this morning, received by telegram from Malad Valley, Samaria, the sorrowful news of the death of our beloved sister Elizabeth. He was conducting the carriage that brought Brigham Young and his companions to Logan; between twelve and one o'clock he brought the grievous news to the family in this part of the country. Our beloved sister departed this life at six o'clock in the morning, peacefully and quietly. She desired her family to come and lay her remains in the earth until the morning of the resurrection. On the seventeenth we began our journey there; we encountered a storm [continues on PDF page 91]

journalPages.welshTranscription:
[continuation from PDF page 90]

a iawn a gwynt oer, ac ni fuom yn alluog i fyned dim pellach na Square Town y dydd hwn. Y 18fed, y tywydd yn lled anhyfryd, a chyrhaeddasom Samaria am ychydig o funudau wedi deg. Wrth edrych ar ei phriod a'i phlant bach, y ty a'r amgylchoedd lle yr oedd wedi bod yn rhodio ac yn amcanu i wneuthur ei hun a'i phriod a'i phlant yn gyffurus, ei mynwes yn oer, y tafod yn fud a'r wefusau yn nghlo, y wedd a'r olwg wedi pellhau, yr yspryd wedi cyfodi ffo ymaith, a dim ond rhyw bridd gwael ac oer oedd i edrych arno, ac yn amser ei roi i orwedd cyn iddo falurio. Am ddau o'r gloch cludwyd ei gweddillion i'r old Hall, lle y cawsom bregeth dda yn Gymraeg gan Owen Thomas, a'r olwg ddiweddaf ar ei gweddillion. Hi a roddodd enedigaeth i saith o blant, tri o fechgyn a phedair o ferched; mae pedwar yn fyw yn bresennol, dau fachgen a dwy ferch. Ar yr ugeinfed (20) cychwynasom dros adref; [unclear: ar un dydd cyrhaeddasom trwy storm i fachgen Conar i dori ei fraich] ychydig uwchlaw ei benelin. Ar yr un dydd, sef 16, a daeth ein chwaer Elizabeth i ymadael a'r fuchedd hon. Mae yn gwella yn dda. Hwn wedi ei ysgrifenu ar y Mehefin 3, 1877.

Medi 4, 1877

Taliesin Hughes a'i chwaer Maria Roberts, a'r eneth ieuanc Elizabeth ein chwaer, a merch ifanc o'r enw Jane Mason, tua deunaw mlwydd ei hoed, a briodwyd hwy gan William B. Preston yn ei dy. Dychwelodd a chyrhaeddasant hyd mor bell a Hamilton Station i dy Ann ein chwaer, lle yr oedd Jane ein chwaer.
journalPages.translation:
[continuation from PDF page 90]

of severe cold and wind, and we were unable to go any farther than Square Town that day. On the eighteenth the weather was rather unpleasant, and we reached Samaria a few minutes after ten. Looking at her husband and her little children, the house and surroundings where she had moved about and sought to make herself, her husband, and her children comfortable, her breast was cold, her tongue silent and her lips closed, her appearance and expression gone, the spirit having risen and fled away, leaving only poor, cold earth to look upon, and it was time to lay it to rest before it crumbled. At about two o'clock her remains were carried to the old Hall, where we heard a good sermon in Welsh by Owen Thomas and took our last look at her remains. She gave birth to seven children, three boys and four girls; four are now living, two boys and two girls. On the twentieth we set out for home. [Uncertain Welsh wording concerning the return journey and Conar's boy breaking his arm a little above the elbow.] On that same day, the sixteenth, our sister Elizabeth departed this life. The boy is recovering well. This was written on June 3, 1877.

September 4, 1877

Taliesin Hughes and his sister Maria Roberts, with the young daughter of our sister Elizabeth, and a young woman named Jane Mason, about eighteen years old, were married by William B. Preston in his house. They returned as far as Hamilton Station, to the house of Ann, our sister, where Jane, our sister, was staying.

journalPages.title: David Roberts Welsh Journal - Page PDF 92
journalPages.pageLanguage: Primarily Welsh; later additions may include English
journalPages.welshTranscription:
Ebrill 10, 1878

Ymadawodd fy anwyl wraig a'r fuchedd hon yn dawel fel i gysgu. Cafodd afiechyd a phoen anghyffredin er dechreu Mawrth, efo'i dannedd i ddechreu; chwyddodd ei chorff yn debyg i'r dropsi. Roedd rhai o'r meddygon yn ei galw yn lled salach ac iawn. Ni chafodd fawr o iechyd ar ol briodi; ymsgariodd a'i bron yn agos i colli ei bywyd pob dro. Mi roedd yn edrych ac yn deimlo yn well y gaeaf hwn nag y bu ers llawer dydd; er hyn i gyd ymaflodd y dinistrwr yn ei chyfansoddiad a gwahanodd yr ysbryd a'r corff. Mi roedd yn wraig ardderchog o lan yn fan a chefnil ac yn medru ei gwaith yn eitha iawn; yn fam rhagorol iawn i'w phlant bach, yn eu dysgu i weddio ac i gydnabod Duw mor fuan ac y byddent yn bosibl; mi roedd yn gymydog cariadus a heddychlon. Ar y deuddegfed (12), am unarddeg o'r gloch (11) y bore, aethom a'i gweddillion i'r hen Hall, lle y cawsom gyfarfod da: gweddi gan Thomas McNeil; pregethau gan John Parry, Robert Davidson a Henry Ballard; diweddiad gan David W. Davies; arweiniwyd y canu gan Alizander Lewis. Claddwyd hi yn mynwent Logan; gweddiwyd gan Benjamin Williams yn y fynwent. Hwn wedi ei ysgrifenu ar y 5ed Mai.

Chwefror 21, 1878

Sarah Ann, gwraig Daniel ein brawd, a rodd enedigaeth i eneth fach am haner awr wedi chwech yn yr hwyr. Mehefin 6 bendithiwyd hi gan Thomas McNeil; ei henw yw Margaret Roberts. Mae yn edrych yn faban clws ac y cyfyd ferch lan [continues on PDF page 93]
journalPages.translation:
April 10, 1878

My beloved wife departed this life peacefully, as though falling asleep. She had suffered unusual illness and pain since the beginning of March, beginning with her teeth; her body swelled as in dropsy. [Some medical wording remains uncertain.] She had little health after marrying and twice miscarried, coming close to losing her life each time. She had looked and felt better this winter than for many days, yet despite everything the destroyer took hold of her constitution and separated spirit from body. She was an excellent, clean, and thrifty wife who managed her work very well; an excellent mother to her little children, teaching them to pray and acknowledge God as soon as they were able; and a loving, peaceable neighbor. On the twelfth, at eleven in the morning, we took her remains to the old Hall, where we had a good meeting: prayer by Thomas McNeil; sermons by John Parry, Robert Davidson, and Henry Ballard; benediction by David W. Davies; singing led by Alizander Lewis. She was buried in the Logan cemetery, where Benjamin Williams offered prayer. This was written on May 5.

February 21, 1878

Sarah Ann, the wife of our brother Daniel, gave birth to a little girl at half past six in the evening. On June 6 she was blessed by Thomas McNeil; her name is Margaret Roberts. She appears to be a pretty baby who will grow into a beautiful girl [continues on PDF page 93]
journalPages.notes:
- The April 1878 obituary and funeral entry has a confirmed close-paraphrase parallel on RDR PDF page 19. RDR expands and smooths several medical and character descriptions; uncertain Welsh medical wording remains cautious here.

[continuation from PDF page 92]

Rhagfyr 29, 1878

Jane ein chwaer, gwraig Conar Hughes, yn byw yn Samaria, a rhodd enedigaeth i fachgan yn edrych yn dda ac yn gryf am bum munud i wyth yn y bore. Ei enw yw Conar Hughes.

Ebrill 3, 1879

Bedyddiwyd David Robert Roberts gan William Waterson; cadarnhawyd ef gan Robert Davidson yr un dydd. Ac hefyd bedyddiwyd David Roberts Hopkin gan Christian L. Larson, a chadarnhawyd ef gan Henry Ballard yr un dydd.

Mai 26, 1879

Am ddeg munud wedi saith yn y bore (10 wedi 7), Ann Hopkin ein chwaer a rodd enedigaeth i fachgen cryf a bywiog yn pwyso deg pwys (10 lbs). Bendithiwyd ef gan Christian L. Larson Gorffenaf 3, 1879; ei enw William John Hopkin.

Mehefin 23, 1879

Am ychydig o funudau i un o'r gloch y prydnawn bu i David Taliesin Hughes farw o glefyd y gwddf ar ol ychydig o dri diwrnod. Aeth yn sal yn yr ysgol fore Gwener a bu farw.

Hyrum Hughes a clafychodd o'r un clefyd ar yr unfed ar hugain (21) o'r un mis [continues on PDF page 94]
journalPages.translation:
[continuation from PDF page 92]

December 29, 1878

Jane, our sister and the wife of Conar Hughes, living in Samaria, gave birth to a boy who looked well and strong at five minutes to eight in the morning. His name is Conar Hughes.

April 3, 1879

David Robert Roberts was baptized by William Waterson and confirmed by Robert Davidson that same day. David Roberts Hopkin was also baptized by Christian L. Larson and confirmed by Henry Ballard that same day.

May 26, 1879

At ten minutes past seven in the morning, Ann Hopkin, our sister, gave birth to a strong and lively boy weighing ten pounds. He was blessed by Christian L. Larson on July 3, 1879; his name is William John Hopkin.

June 23, 1879

A few minutes before one in the afternoon, David Taliesin Hughes died of a throat disease after an illness of about three days. He became ill at school on Friday morning and died.

Hyrum Hughes became ill with the same disease on the twenty-first of the same month [continues on PDF page 94]

Logan City, Hydref 4, 1879

Sarah Ann Roberts, gwraig Daniel Roberts, a rhodd enedigaeth i ferch fechan yn yr hwyr am un o'r gloch y prydnawn, yn pwyso 9 lbs. Rhagfyr 4 bendithiwyd hi gan Thomas McNeil; ei henw yw Ida Roberts.

Awst 5, 1880

Sarah Ann, gwraig Daniel Roberts, a fedyddiwyd ar unwaith gan Christian L. Larson. Cadarnhawyd hi gan Henry Ballard.

Chwefror 19, 1881

Thomas J. Roberts a ail fedyddiwyd gan Henry Ballard; cadarnhawyd ef gan yr un. Ac ar y 24ain, fe a'i amcanwraig Margaret Davies a aethant i Dy yr Arglwydd yn Ninas y Llyn Halen, a unwyd yn nghwlwm y cyfamod tragwyddol i fod yn wr a gwraig am amser ac am dragwyddoldeb gan Daniel H. Wells.

Margaret yn cael ei hindowment ar yr un pryd [continues on PDF page 95]
journalPages.translation:
[continuation from PDF page 93]

and died at about two o'clock in the morning on the twenty-fifth. He had been very ill with the disease. Born on March 6, 1874, the two were fine boys who appeared likely to grow into strong young men. They were buried in Samaria, Oneida County, Idaho Territory, where their father lives.

Logan City, October 4, 1879

Sarah Ann Roberts, the wife of Daniel Roberts, gave birth to a little girl at about one o'clock in the afternoon, weighing nine pounds. On December 4 she was blessed by Thomas McNeil; her name is Ida Roberts.

August 5, 1880

Sarah Ann, the wife of Daniel Roberts, was rebaptized by Christian L. Larson. She was confirmed by Henry Ballard.

February 19, 1881

Thomas J. Roberts was rebaptized by Henry Ballard and confirmed by the same man. Margaret received her endowment at the same time [continues on PDF page 95]

journalPages.title: David Roberts Welsh Journal - Page PDF 95
journalPages.pageLanguage: Primarily Welsh; later additions may include English
journalPages.welshTranscription:
[continuation from PDF page 94]

Miss Davies a aned yn Rhosllanerchrugog, Cymru, yn Sir Ddinbych, 30 Mehefin 1854.

Bedyddiwyd hi gan Henry Hatfield yn Liverpool. Cadarnhawyd gan Joseph H. Smith, Awst 1877.

Ymfudodd i Utah yn y flwyddyn 1878, a chyrhaeddodd Dinas y Llyn Halen ac arhosodd hi efo teulu Mr William Williams, Kensington, nes yr oedd yn Ebrill 1880, pan y daeth hi a'i chwaer Polly, yr hon a ymfudodd yn y flwyddyn 1879 i Ddinas y Llyn Halen, pan y daethant i Logan a rhentu lle bychan gan Mrs W. H. Garry, ac yr oedd yn cadw busnes gwnio lle y maent yn bresennol.

Ei rhieni yw Robert ac Ann Davies. Bedyddiwyd hwy yn Rhosllanerchrugog, Cymru, yn y flwyddyn 1855 gan John Berry, Elder. Yn Ebrill y flwyddyn 1858 daethant i fyw i Manchester.

Yn y flwyddyn 1860 daethant i fyw i Liverpool, ac ymfudasant o Liverpool i Utah Hydref 18, 1879, a chyrhaeddasant Utah, Logan, Tachwedd 10, 1879.

Mae dau fab a thair neu bedair o ferched yn y wlad eto heb ddod yma eto.
journalPages.translation:
[continuation from PDF page 94]

Miss Davies was born in Rhosllanerchrugog, Denbighshire, Wales, on June 30, 1854.

She was baptized by Henry Hatfield in Liverpool and confirmed by Joseph H. Smith in August 1877.

She emigrated to Utah in 1878 and arrived in Salt Lake City, where she stayed with the family of Mr. William Williams in Kensington until April 1880. Then she and her sister Polly, who had emigrated to Salt Lake City in 1879, came to Logan and rented a small place from Mrs. W. H. Garry, where they kept a sewing business and remain at present.

Her parents are Robert and Ann Davies. They were baptized in Rhosllanerchrugog, Wales, in 1855 by Elder John Berry. In April 1858 they moved to Manchester.

In 1860 they moved to Liverpool, and on October 18, 1879, they emigrated from Liverpool to Utah, arriving in Logan, Utah, on November 10, 1879.

Two sons and three or four daughters remain in the old country and have not yet come here.
journalPages.notes:

- No occurrence of `bach` or a distinct Robert-derived nickname is visible on pages 92–95.
- Handwriting continuity supports probable attribution to Robert D. Roberts as content author and scribe. No signature or secondary hand appears.

Am chwech yn yr hwyr Jane Hughes ein chwaer a rodd enedigaeth i ferch fechan yn pwyso 4 pwys. Mae y fam a'r ferch yn cymeryd yn dda. Ganwyd hi yn Denbigh, Ontario County, Belle Farmley.

Logan City Hydref 21ain 1881

March 22, 1881

At six in the evening, our sister Jane Hughes gave birth to a little girl weighing four pounds. The mother and daughter are doing well. She was born in Denbigh, Ontario County, Belle Farmley.

Logan City, October 21, 1881

At fifteen minutes past three in the morning (3:15 a.m.), Sarah Ann Roberts, wife of Daniel Roberts, gave birth to a fine daughter weighing ten and a half pounds. She was blessed on December 5 by Christian L. Larson and named Ann Roberts.

Logan City, December 26, 1881

At fifty-five minutes past seven in the morning, Margaret Goodman, wife of Thomas J. Roberts, gave birth to a fine son weighing nine pounds. He was blessed by Thomas McNeil on March 2, 1882, and named David William Roberts.

Logan City, November 13, 1882

In the Third Ward, David Robert Roberts was ordained by Robert Davidson to the office of deacon in the Aaronic Priesthood.

journalPages.welshTranscription:
Logan City Chwefror 1af 1883

Mi anfonodd lythyr at [unclear: deulu ni] Conar Hughes yn ein hysbysu fod ei wraig Jane, ein chwaer, wedi rhoi genedigaeth i fachgen ar Ionawr 17eg 1883 am ugain munud wedi un (20.1) yn y bore. Bendithiwyd ef gan David R. Bowen Mawrth 1af, ei enw Robert Richard Hughes.

Logan City Ionawr 4ydd 1884

Er cofawdriaeth am Robert Davies a aned yn Rhuthun, Sir Ddinbych, Cymru, Chwefror 25ain 1819. Bedyddiwyd ef yn Rhuthun gan John Parry yn y flwyddyn 1853. Bu farw yn Logan City Ionawr 2ail 1884 am ddeng munud wedi un yn y bore (1.10). Claddwyd ef ar y 3ydd. Agorwyd y cwrdd gan yr Esgob Henry Ballard, cyhoeddwyd gan Georg Painter, bregethwyd gan yr Esgob Ballard. Ei gynghorwyr Christian L. Larson mewn modd dymunol a chymerth amrywiaeth o ganiadau gan Georg Morrison, diweddiwyd gan John Thomas. Gwasanaenwyd y te gan Christian L. Larson.

Robert Davies yw dad ynghyfraith Thomas J. Roberts.
journalPages.translation:
Logan City, February 1, 1883

Conar Hughes sent a letter to [unclear in Welsh], informing us that his wife Jane, our sister, had given birth to a boy on January 17, 1883, at twenty minutes past one in the morning. He was blessed by David R. Bowen on March 1 and named Robert Richard Hughes.

Logan City, January 4, 1884

In memory of Robert Davies, who was born in Ruthin, Denbighshire, Wales, on February 25, 1819. He was baptized in Ruthin by John Parry in 1853. He died in Logan City on January 2, 1884, at ten minutes past one in the morning. He was buried on the third. The meeting was opened by Bishop Henry Ballard; [unclear in Welsh] by Georg Painter; Bishop Ballard preached. His counselor Christian L. Larson [spoke] in a pleasing manner, and a variety of songs were provided by Georg Morrison. John Thomas closed the meeting. Tea was served by Christian L. Larson.

Logan City, January 5, 1895

William John Hopkins was baptized by Charles Limberg and confirmed by John Talley.

Logan City, April 9, 1888

I received a letter from Samaria from Conar Hughes informing us that Jane, our sister and his wife, had given birth to a little girl weighing ten pounds on March 31 at fifteen minutes past twelve in the morning (12:15 midnight).

We note a communication from Samaria dated May 3, 1888, informing us that the little girl born in April 1888 to Conar and our sister Jane Hughes had been blessed by Bishop Jonah Evans on May 3, 1888; her name was Cathrine Roberts Hughes.

Logan City, October 17, 1897

Thomas D. Roberts set out on his journey to Wales, from his [unclear Welsh travel/mission wording concerning departure from Salt Lake City].
